agent_instructions.instruction: Resolve retailer first. Search retailer-specific private-label canonical brands/aliases, then Regional/National canonical brands/aliases, then queue an unknown.
Never treat a retailer private label as globally matching outside its retailer context unless an explicit cross-retailer comparison is being generated.
A Regional/National brand exists once canonically. Retailer availability is a separate relationship/evidence layer.
Retailer_Presence_Seed value UNKNOWN means not yet verified. It must never be interpreted as absent or unavailable.

For regional_brand candidates, geographic overlap between product/store location and core_region increases confidence; out-of-region observations should trigger evidence review, not automatic rejection.

agent_instructions.topic: National is not universal shelf presence
agent_instructions.instruction: national_brand means broad brand distribution, not proof that every retailer or location currently carries the brand.
Milk, Eggs, Cheese and Yogurt are high-priority matching categories. Do not use brand similarity to cross these category boundaries without explicit product taxonomy evidence.
Milk matching should distinguish dairy vs plant-based, fat level, organic, lactose-free, A2/A2, ultra-filtered, flavored, shelf-stable/refrigerated and package size.
Egg matching should distinguish shell vs prepared/alternative, grade, size, color, cage-free/free-range/pasture-raised/organic, count and specialty claims.
Cheese matching should distinguish cheese type/style, natural vs processed vs plant-based, format (block/shred/slice/string/spread), milk type, flavor and weight.
Yogurt matching should distinguish traditional/Greek/skyr/Australian/Bulgarian/plant-based, fat level, protein positioning, organic, flavor, multipack/count and package size.
Do not collapse parent-company brands into one consumer brand. DFA, Lactalis, Danone, Cal-Maine and similar portfolios intentionally retain distinct consumer-facing canonical brands.
Run exact normalized canonical and alias matching before fuzzy matching. Category-qualified short aliases require the category_context gate.
Fuzzy similarity may propose candidates but cannot automatically merge distinct brands, especially short names or geographically distinct regional brands.
Owner/marketer, brand bucket and distribution_scope are separate facts. An owned brand may be regional; a licensed brand may be national.
New scrape brands enter Candidate/Unknown unless they resolve deterministically. Scraping does not directly create an approved Regional/National classification.

When a Regional/National brand is observed at Walmart, ALDI, H-E-B, Target, Kroger or Whole Foods, update the retailer-brand relationship evidence with first_seen/last_seen rather than duplicating the brand.
Use last_verified_at and retailer presence last_seen dates. Brand ownership, distribution and retailer assortment can change.
For Milk/Eggs/Cheese/Yogurt, prefer first-party brand/corporate evidence and product-category evidence over secondary brand lists.
Treat the master as a high-coverage foundation, not a claim that every U.S. grocery brand has been enumerated. Unknown discoveries are expected and should improve the master.
